threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'sourdough' is just a type of bread, not a lifestyle choice. The locals have strong opinions about their loaves.
Last night on the 59, a guy tried to sell me a 'genuine' ticket stub for a vanished concert. The bus driver just shook his head and kept driving.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The way the Turkish bakery fills with laughter and the smell of fresh simit at sunrise—it's like the heartbeat of the neighborhood waking up.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find bars where they serve beer in plastic cups during summer festivals while charging extra for the proper glasses. Classic!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can tell you which taco truck has the best al pastor without even thinking twice.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 47 this morning, and a guy dressed as a giant avocado serenaded us with ukulele covers. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can find 'authentic' paella everywhere. The locals know it’s a weekend dish, best enjoyed by the sea, not in the neighborhood tapas bars.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still check their Metro map at every stop. Locals know the shortcuts and the buses are just a glance away.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think all the coffee shops serve 'regular' sizes instead of 'small,' 'medium,' and 'large.' It’s a tell.
Last week, a guy was trying to impress his date on the bus, turned up the radio on his phone, only to get busted by the driver for noise. Awkward silence followed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: That moment when you realize the kebab shop staff know your order by heart, and you can hear their banter through the window while you wait.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a Kebab shop that doubles as a punk music venue at midnight. Gritty, loud, and deliciously unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they casually mention the smell of burnt toast from the BART tube—just part of the commute, not a surprise.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus driver in the Tenderloin singing along to the radio, completely unbothered by the chaos around. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the 'pommes frites' at the kiosks are the local snack. True locals grab a 'bocata' from the corner bars instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their puzzled expressions at the bus stops, still trying to decipher the irregular schedules.
